requirement:
After a rejection under {cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.rejection`,
a submission whose previously flagged rationale is exactly the UUID that rejection gave MUST
resolve to the rejected submission unchanged, ignoring the new submission's
other fields; acceptance remains subject to
{cite}`requirements.authoring.submission.searches.line_numbers`. After passing that gate, any other rationale that cites line numbers MUST fail
the assessment, so
an assessment rejects at most one submission. The UUID MUST NOT be recorded in
evidence.
rationale:
structural: Every clause of `requirements.authoring.line_numbers.resubmission` specifies observable harness behavior. None prescribes a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or named interface for the implementation.

- "a submission whose previously flagged rationale is exactly the UUID that rejection gave MUST resolve to the rejected submission unchanged, ignoring the new submission's other fields" is an input/output rule. The harness could keep the rejected submission in a map, a field, or a closure, or re-parse it. All of these give the same result.
- "acceptance remains subject to `requirements.authoring.submission.searches.line_numbers`" is a behavioral ordering of gates. It is not a prescribed call structure. The cited requirement only says the outstanding-search check runs before rationale vetting, and that a submission rejected for an outstanding search leaves the correction attempt available. Both are observable outcomes.
- "any other rationale that cites line numbers MUST fail the assessment, so an assessment rejects at most one submission" is a behavioral outcome.
- "The UUID MUST NOT be recorded in evidence" is a constraint on output content. It is not a structural constraint.

Any alternative internal design that produces the same results still satisfies the text, so the implementation choices are discretionary. No implementation roots are supplied, and none are needed as structural evidence. Behavioral verification is left to the test-adequacy criterion.

behavioral: I found no test-adequacy gap in the reviewed tests. I did not read the implementation.

**Resolves to the rejected submission, other fields ignored.**
- `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_rejection_gives_a_uuid_that_keeps_the_rejected_submission]` rejects a cited submission and takes the UUID from the message. It then resubmits with `determination: true` and `rationale` set to the UUID, where the rejected submission had `determination: false`. It asserts `resubmitted` returns exactly the original `cited` value, so the new submission's other fields are ignored and the original is unchanged.
- The same test resubmits `"{uuid} "` with a trailing space and asserts `None`, which covers the "exactly the UUID" boundary.
- It also asserts that `resubmitted` returns `None` before any rejection has been made.

**Position for `Failed`.**
- `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[uuid_restores_only_at_the_rejected_correction_position]` rejects a `Failed` submission whose flagged rationale is correction 1.
- It asserts the message names `/corrections/1/rationale`.
- It asserts the UUID at correction position 0 returns `None`.
- It asserts the UUID at position 1 restores the original.

**Any other line-numbered rationale fails, so at most one rejection.**
- In `a_rejection_gives_a_uuid_that_keeps_the_rejected_submission`, a clean resubmission after the rejection is `Accept`.
- Resubmitting the cited rationale again returns `Outcome::Fail` with a message containing "after a rejection".
- `uuid_restores_only_at_the_rejected_correction_position` also asserts `Outcome::Fail` for a repeated citing submission.
- Each rejection gives a fresh UUID: a second `Rejection` produces a message that does not contain the first UUID.

**Acceptance remains subject to the outstanding-search gate.**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[keeping_a_rejected_rationale_waits_for_search_and_preserves_the_original_verdict]` runs the full flow.
- The model submits a line-numbered rationale, then makes a search call. It then tries to keep the rationale while the search is outstanding.
- The test asserts the tool reply mentions `finish_search`. After the search is finished, the keep is accepted.

**Original verdict preserved and UUID not recorded.**
- The same CLI test asserts the evidence record has `determination` true and the original rationale text.
- It extracts the UUID from the correction message and asserts it does not appear anywhere in the serialized record.

The gate-ordering clause ("after passing that gate") orders the checks. Its search-gate side is covered by the CLI test above. The gate's own behaviour belongs to `requirements.authoring.submission.searches.line_numbers`, which I did not reassess.

text: :::{req} line_numbers.resubmission
After a rejection under {cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.rejection`,
a submission whose previously flagged rationale is exactly the UUID that rejection gave MUST
resolve to the rejected submission unchanged, ignoring the new submission's
other fields; acceptance remains subject to
{cite}`requirements.authoring.submission.searches.line_numbers`. After passing that gate, any other rationale that cites line numbers MUST fail
the assessment, so
an assessment rejects at most one submission. The UUID MUST NOT be recorded in
evidence.
:::{req} line_numbers.rejection
For requirement, example, and site reviews, when the only submission in a response
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.submission` is otherwise valid but any of its
rationales cites line numbers under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.detection`, and it is the
assessment's first such submission, and it passes the outstanding-search gate
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.submission.searches.line_numbers`, the
harness MUST reject it instead of
accepting it and continue the conversation. The tool result MUST quote the
matched text, identify the affected rationale (including its correction position
for `Failed`), repeat the location guidance of
{cite}`requirements.authoring.judgment_rules`, and give a fresh random UUID,
saying the model may submit once more, either without line numbers or with
the offending rationale set to exactly that UUID to keep the rejected submission as it was.
A rejection MUST be counted in usage like any other turn.
:::{req} submission.searches.line_numbers

The SDK checks for outstanding searches before invoking Habeas's rationale vetting. A submission rejected for an outstanding search MUST leave the rationale correction attempt available under {cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.rejection`.
